name: a_ai_policy
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: AI policy & safety.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Government actions on AI (White House, Congress, EU, UK, China), AI safety statements by named executives, antitrust actions against tech platforms, court rulings affecting tech.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **NVDA** [AI Safety · AI Compute]
- CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia would hypothetically stop supplying chips to a customer developing unsafe AI software, after first discussing the issue with the customer; he also said AI-safety concerns were “overdone.” Nvidia committed \( \$250 \) million over five years in computing access for UK AI-safety research. (Business Times, Oct 15 07:54 ET)[6]

## Anthropic [AI Safety · Software & SaaS]
- Anthropic selected METR and SecureBio to evaluate its AI-safety practices and said the evaluators would help verify compliance; Accenture was identified as its first partner. (CNBC, Oct 15 16:35 ET)[5]
- New York City Comptroller Mark Levine urged CEO Dario Amodei to pause Anthropic’s IPO until the company addresses AI-safety, governance and development-speed risks, and requested specific disclosures on audits, controls and implementation timelines. [report] (Bloomberg, Oct 15; time not stated)[4][7]

## White House [AI Policy]
- The White House Super Intelligence Task Force was scheduled to hold its first meeting at 16:00 ET on Oct. 15, with more than a dozen Cabinet members and senior officials expected; the group is chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, with Scott Kupor, Emil Michael and FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson as vice chairs. (Politico, Oct 15 15:14 ET)[3]
- The task force’s stated approach centers on applying existing civil and criminal liability laws to AI companies rather than creating new regulations; its goals and responsibilities were expected after the initial meeting. (Politico, Oct 15 15:14 ET)[3]

## TikTok / **BDN** [Internet & Platforms · Antitrust]
- Advocate General Andrea Biondi recommended that the EU Court of Justice dismiss ByteDance’s challenge to TikTok’s designation as a Digital Markets Act gatekeeper, a status carrying obligations intended to limit anti-competitive practices; the opinion was not the final court ruling. (Reuters, Oct 15; time not stated)[1]

## China, United States and EU [AI Policy · Geopolitics]
- China, the United States, the European Union and more than 25 countries signed the Bletchley Declaration, agreeing to cooperate on identifying shared AI risks, developing scientific understanding and creating cross-border mitigation policies. (Economic Times, Oct 15; time not stated)[2]

## Meta [Internet & Platforms · Antitrust]
- The FTC said it would appeal a U.S. district-court ruling that rejected its antitrust case against Meta, maintaining that Meta unlawfully maintained a social-networking monopoly through its acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp; the ruling had rejected the FTC’s request for structural relief. (Economic Times, Oct 15; time not stated)[10]
